paper_title: Formalisation and Extension of Lagois Connections for Secure Information Flow
classifications: Security and privacy → Formal methods and theory of security
statement: Two concepts that our framework does not account for is dynamism of agents (à la Nielson et al. [8, 9]) and dynamism of policies (à la Askarov and Chong [1]). By dynamism of agents we mean the ability of agents to move about in the network and in the process dropping old connections and establishing new ones. For example [9] has dynamism of agents: Agents can move between clusters of agents via a primitive relocate(l) command, that relocates agent v to cluster l when executed at agent v. By dynamism of policies we mean the ability of policies to change during runtime. Conversely [1] has dynamism of policies: A program can update its information flow policy via a setPolicy(⊑) primitive for some reflexive relation ⊑. We conjecture that our framework may be expanded to cover both types of dynamism using dependent functions:   G →G G′ = (v ∈ G) → (v ′ ∈ G) × L(v) → L(v ′ ) . (19)

Two concepts that our framework does not account for is dynamism of agents (à la Nielson et al. [8, 9]) and dynamism of policies (à la Askarov and Chong [1]). By dynamism of agents we mean the ability of agents to move about in the network and in the process dropping old connections and establishing new ones. For example [9] has dynamism of agents: Agents can move between clusters of agents via a primitive relocate(l) command, that relocates agent v to cluster l when executed at agent v. By dynamism of policies we mean the ability of policies to change during runtime. Conversely [1] has dynamism of policies: A program can update its information flow policy via a setPolicy(⊑) primitive for some reflexive relation ⊑. We conjecture that our framework may be expanded to cover both types of dynamism using dependent functions:   G →G G′ = (v ∈ G) → (v ′ ∈ G) × L(v) → L(v ′ ) . (19) For F ∈ G →G G′ and v ∈ G we would then interpret F (v) as v moving to or becoming π1 (F (v)) and v’s lattice transforming as specified by π2 (F (v)). More specifically π2 (F (v))(p) = p′ would denote label p becoming label p′ . We leave this for future work. Finally, we would like to thank the reviewers for their detailed, constructive, and very helpful feedback.
